extracted.intended_audience: users of the GAP computer algebra system who want to read and navigate GAP's documentation/help from within a GAP session
extracted.subtask_description: How to invoke and browse GAP's interactive help, configure which viewers are used (screen, web browser, PDF viewers, text-based browsers), and how to use the built-in pager. Covers command syntax, navigation commands, viewer selection, and pager configuration/options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help query syntax and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the form ?[book:][topic] with the first question mark in the first position after the gap> prompt. The search strings book and topic are normalized before searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization: remove backslashes and double/single quotes; substitute parentheses and braces by blanks; treat non-ASCII characters as ISO-latin1 and replace accented letters by their non-accented counterparts; normalize white space. The search is case-insensitive and arbitrary whitespace is allowed after the first question mark. If multiple manual sections match, a numbered list is shown and matches can be accessed with ?number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browsing/navigation commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Special single-character help commands starting with ? allow chapter/section-wise browsing and history navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands include: ?< (previous section/subsection), ?> (next section/subsection), ?<< (beginning of current chapter or previous chapter if already at start), ?>> (beginning of next chapter), ?- (go back in the history of viewed sections), ?+ (go forward in that history). Note: ?- and ?+ do not alter the history like the other commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help books and tables of contents commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands to list known help books and show their tables of contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ?books to show the list of books known to the help system; for each book a short name (for use in help queries) and a long name are shown. A short name ending with (not loaded) refers to a GAP package whose documentation is loaded but which requires LoadPackage before its functions can be used. Use ?[book:]sections or ?[book:][chapters] to show tables of contents for available/matching books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redisplaying last shown section with preferred viewer
rubrics_metrics.description: The commands ? and ?& redisplay the last shown help section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the form ?& the next preferred help viewer is used for the display (if several viewers were chosen), see SetHelpViewer. ? (without &) simply redisplays the last shown section in the current viewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default display behavior and help formats
rubrics_metrics.description: By default GAP shows help sections as text in the terminal, page by page if the text doesn't fit the screen. Help books may also be available in pdf or HTML formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text format is used for terminal display (Pager). PDF is suitable for printing/onscreen reading and may contain hyperlinks. HTML is usable with web browsers and may contain hyperlink cross-references. Limitations: complicated mathematical expressions may be hard to read in text and HTML; older manuals may use special symbol fonts requiring browser configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetHelpViewer: configuring preferred viewers and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: SetHelpViewer(viewer1, viewer2, ...) sets an ordered list of viewer names; the first available format for a section is chosen according to this priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A call with no arguments shows the current setting. The first arguments have higher priority. The viewer "screen" is silently appended to the list because each help book is assumed to be available in text format. To change defaults persistently, set the user preference "HelpViewers" in gap.ini via SetUserPreference("HelpViewers", [...]). ?& will attempt to use the next possible viewer in your list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized viewers and their behavior/limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The help system recognizes several viewer names that map to particular programs or display methods (screen, web browsers, text browsers, PDF viewers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and notes: "screen" shows text via Pager (default); "firefox", "chrome", "mozilla", "netscape", "konqueror" open HTML books in the corresponding web browser (may depend on start scripts and symbol font configuration); "browser" on Windows opens the default HTML application; "links2", "w3m", "lynx" display HTML in text-mode browsers inside the terminal (formulae using special symbol fonts may be unreadable); macOS options include "mac default browser", "safari", "firefox"; "xpdf" opens PDF on X window systems and is reusable for subsequent displays; "acroread" opens PDF but cannot be started at a given page and will print page numbers instead; macOS PDF options include "pdf viewer", "skim", "preview", "adobe reader" — only Skim seems to support opening a PDF at a given page (named destination support is limited across viewers). Send ideas for further viewer commands to support@gap-system.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to prefer external pagers on UNIX
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP contains a builtin pager but recommends using an external pager like less or more on UNIX systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the user preference "Pager" to "less" or "more" (e.g., SetUserPreference("Pager", "less");) and optionally configure "PagerOptions" (e.g., SetUserPreference("PagerOptions", ["-f","-r","-a","-i","-M","-j2"]);). GAP assumes external pagers support +nr and +/str options to start display at a given line number or search string.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pager function and its purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Pager(lines) displays a text string page-by-page using GAP's pager; the builtin pager is rudimentary but portable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pager is used by the help system for displaying text-format help sections. The default builtin pager has limited capabilities; on systems with powerful external pagers, prefer configuring GAP to use them via the "Pager" user preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pager argument forms and record components
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pager function accepts (1) a string (lines separated by newlines), (2) a list of strings (each a line), or (3) a record with component lines (and optional extra components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a record, optional components include: formatted (true/false) — if true the builtin pager tries to show the text exactly as given, avoiding GAP's automatic line breaking; start — positive integer or string: integer is the first line number to show, string is a search string and the pager shows starting from the first line containing it; exitAtEnd — false/true (default true): if true the builtin pager terminates at end of text, otherwise user must press 'q' to exit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pager start behavior and exitAtEnd
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of the 'start' and 'exitAtEnd' record fields passed to Pager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: start as integer: number of the first line shown; start as string: search string for first line to show (back scrolling may show earlier lines). exitAtEnd default true: builtin pager returns automatically when end is reached; set false to require 'q' to return from the pager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal display recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Text versions of manuals are formatted assuming at least 80 characters per line and a fixed-width font; UTF-8 encoding is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If terminal width is less than 80 characters, some sections may display poorly. Suggest using a terminal in UTF-8 encoding with a fixed-width font (default on modern systems); ISO-8859-X encoding terminals will also work reasonably well for now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package documentation availability indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: A short name ending in (not loaded) signals a GAP package documentation that is known but requires explicit loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a book's short name ends with (not loaded) you must call LoadPackage(...) before you can use the described functions in that package.
